messages.author: Martin Rosellen
messages.body:
Dear all,
I read the chapter on GB in the Amber manual and understood that one can
do configurational entropy calculations using quasi-harmonic or normal
mode approximation. My question is if there is a part in the mmpbsa.py
script that approximates the entropy of hydrophobic interactions? I also
had a look at the OBC papers for gb=2 but could not find any information
if that is the case. Could you point me to the appropriate paper or
paragraph in the manual please?
cheers
Martin

messages.author: David Case
messages.body:
On Wed, Jan 08, 2020, Martin Rosellen wrote:
>
>My question is if there is a part in the mmpbsa.py
>script that approximates the entropy of hydrophobic interactions?
No. Just like there is nothing that tries to figure out the entropy of
electrostatic interactions. GB numbers are estimates of free energies only.
Note 1: the configurational entropy calculation is a completely
different beast, and has nothing to do with implicit solvation models.
Note 2: the 3D-RSIM implicit solvent model does provide estimates of
enthalpy and entropy (as well as free energy) for all interaction types.
I would characterize the results for test cases we have made a "OK but
not great". To draw your own conclusions, see:
J. Johnson, D.A. Case, T. Yamazaki, S. Gusarov, A. Kovalenko
and T. Luchko. Small Molecule Solvation Energy and Entropy from
3D-RISM. J. Phys. Cond. Mat. 28, 344002 (2016).
....dac

messages.author: Rosellen, Martin
messages.body:
Hi David,
thanks for the clarification.
In the Amber tutorial on MMGBSA
http://ambermd.org/tutorials/advanced/tutorial3/
there is an empirical term for hydrophobic contributions mentioned. As I understand you this does not related to entropy at all?
best
Martin

messages.author: Carlos Simmerling
messages.body:
A surface area term is a simple approximation for nonpolar solvation
effects. A portion of that arises from water entropy. So yes, this is
related to water entropy, but perhaps not in a very quantitative way.
